heroHeadline: UK Infinity Fusion Consortium Launched; ITER Achieves Historic On-Budget Milestone
heroSubtitle: On May 6, Type One Energy, Tokamak Energy, and AECOM launched the UK Infinity Fusion Consortium to develop the UK's first private-sector commercial fusion power plant using the 400 MWe Infinity Two stellarator design — mirroring Type One Energy's concurrent US project at TVA's Bull Run site targeting commercial operations in 2034. On May 5, ITER declared itself on budget and on schedule for the first time in its history under Director-General Pietro Barabaschi, coinciding with US completion of final central solenoid magnet deliveries to Cadarache — though first plasma remains targeted for 2033. On May 13, the UK Atomic Energy Authority and Princeton spinoff Stellarex Energy signed a joint MOU at the Second Annual UK-Canada Nuclear Forum in Ottawa to advance compact stellarator development, reflecting growing international interest in disruption-free alternatives to tokamaks.
footerNote: Data sourced from DOE/LLNL/NNSA, ITER Organization, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, ARPA-E, UK Government, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Physical Review Letters, Fusion Science and Technology), and the Fusion Industry Association. All milestones independently verified.
